compare:0.en: The troupe's map room smelled of old ink and rain. Old Helm spread two torn charts across the table and began to *compare* them side by side, searching for the route through the storm waters. 'Look,' he said softly. 'The safe channel is where both maps agree.'
compare:0.cnHint: 老舵把两张破损的海图放在一起____，试图找出穿越风暴海域的安全航线。
compare:0.hook: But one map showed a passage that the other had erased.
compare:0.line: 'Always *compare* two charts before you trust either one,' Old Helm said.

past:0.en: Bell sat quietly in the corner of the ship's cabin, turning an old coin in her fingers. She rarely spoke about her *past*, but tonight the storm outside made her remember the island she had left behind as a child, and a sadness settled briefly on her face before she smiled again.
past:0.cnHint: 小铃独自坐在船舱一角，回想着她那段很少提及的____。
past:0.hook: The coin bore a name none of us had ever seen on any map.
past:0.line: 'My *past* is a place I can visit, but never live in again,' Bell said.

suffer:0.en: The cabin shook as wind slammed the outer walls. Old Helm told us that ships entering the storm waters without a proper word-fragment would *suffer* badly — spinning in fog, losing all sense of direction, sometimes for days. He tapped the table. 'We will not make that mistake tonight.'
suffer:0.cnHint: 老舵警告大家，没有词语碎片就进入风暴海域的船只会____惨重。
suffer:0.hook: Then the lantern above us swung hard, and everything went dark.
suffer:0.line: 'No one should *suffer* the fog twice — once teaches you enough,' Old Helm said.

almost:0.en: Bell traced the storm route with one careful finger. The narrow passage between the two cloud-islands was *almost* too tight for our vessel, she said, measuring the gap against the ship's width drawn on the chart. She bit her lip. 'We can make it, but only if the wind stays kind.'
almost:0.cnHint: 小铃仔细测量后发现，两座云岛之间的通道____不够宽，让大家捏了一把汗。
almost:0.hook: A low growl of thunder answered her words from somewhere very close.
almost:0.line: 'We have *almost* everything we need — find that last word-fragment,' Bell said.

especially:0.en: Old Helm handed out warm cups of broth before the night watch began. He always cared for the troupe's spirits before a hard crossing, *especially* when the younger members were nervous. He walked from bunk to bunk, said a quiet word to each of us, and left the cabin smelling of ginger and calm.
especially:0.cnHint: 老舵总是在艰难航行前照顾大家的情绪，____关心年轻成员。
especially:0.hook: He paused at my bunk the longest, and said nothing at all.
especially:0.line: 'Rest well, *especially* you — tomorrow will ask a lot of you,' Old Helm said.

publish:0.en: Tucked behind a loose board in the cabin wall, Bell found a small hand-bound book. Its cover read: 'Storm Charts — do not *publish*.' She opened it gently. Every page mapped a different floating island hidden inside the storm waters, drawn in ink so fine it looked like spider silk.
publish:0.cnHint: 小铃在船舱墙板后发现了一本封面写着"请勿____"的手绘航海图册。
publish:0.hook: The last page had our ship's name written in someone else's hand.
publish:0.line: 'Whoever chose not to *publish* this wanted to keep these islands secret,' Bell said.

activity:0.en: Through the round cabin window we could see the storm wall ahead, lit from inside by pale flickers. Old Helm pressed his ear to the glass and listened. 'There is *activity* in there,' he murmured, 'movement, not just wind — something is alive inside that cloud.' Nobody spoke for a long moment.
activity:0.cnHint: 老舵贴着舷窗细听，察觉到风暴云层内部有不寻常的____。
activity:0.hook: Then a shape, huge and slow, drifted past the glass.
activity:0.line: 'That kind of *activity* inside a storm cloud means we are not alone,' Old Helm said.

science:0.en: Silverfang arrived uninvited, ducking through our cabin door with rain on her coat. She dropped a folder on the table — pages dense with numbers and diagrams. 'I mapped the storm using *science*,' she said, tapping a formula at the top. 'Currents, pressure, ion charge. I know the safest second.' Old Helm raised one eyebrow.
science:0.cnHint: 银牙突然闯入船舱，声称用____方法绘制出了穿越风暴的最优路线。
science:0.hook: Old Helm's old chart and her numbers pointed to opposite directions entirely.
science:0.line: '*Science* found the gap in the storm — now let us see if luck agrees,' Silverfang said.

contribute:0.en: Rain hammered the roof of the old chart house. Inside, Bell spread her maps across the table and asked each of us to *contribute* one detail we had noticed during the crossing — a current, a colour in the clouds, a smell on the wind. Every small piece helped complete the picture.
contribute:0.cnHint: 小铃让每个人把观察到的细节____到地图绘制中。
contribute:0.hook: One detail did not match anything on any known chart.
contribute:0.line: 'Even a single star sighting can *contribute* more than you think,' Bell said.

share:0.en: Old Helm divided the last of the warm soup into three bowls, making sure each *share* was equal. The storm outside shook the walls, but inside the chart house the three of us sat close, listening to the wind and saying very little. Some silences feel like company.
share:0.cnHint: 老船长把汤分成三份，每人得到平等的一____。
share:0.hook: Then Old Helm set down his bowl and reached for the sealed map.
share:0.line: 'Your *share* is the same as mine — no more, no less,' Old Helm said.

decade:0.en: Bell traced a faded line on the oldest chart and told us that no troupe had sailed this route in over a *decade*. The ink had gone pale, the island names were half worn away, and two of the marked anchorages no longer existed. Time, she said, is its own kind of wind.
decade:0.cnHint: 小铃说这条航线已经超过一个____没有船队走过了。
decade:0.hook: Yet someone had pencilled a fresh mark near the storm's centre.
decade:0.line: 'A *decade* of silence on this route — that alone should warn us,' Bell said.

kind:0.en: The chart house held every *kind* of weather record the troupe had gathered over the years — rain logs, wind roses, pressure notes on scraps of cloth. Old Helm ran his hand along the shelves with quiet pride. 'Each one,' he said, 'was someone's careful hour.'
kind:0.cnHint: 图表室里收藏着各种各样____的天气记录。
kind:0.hook: But the record for tonight's storm was completely blank.
kind:0.line: 'I have never seen this *kind* of pressure drop before,' Old Helm admitted.

across:0.en: Lightning flashed and for one bright moment I could see *across* the full width of the storm through the chart-house window — rolling black clouds, a spinning funnel of wind, and far beyond it, a thin line of gold where the sky was still clear. Then darkness returned.
across:0.cnHint: 闪电亮起，我透过窗户看____了整片风暴。
across:0.hook: That gold line held the shape of an island no chart had named.
across:0.line: 'Look *across* the cloud wall — do you see that light?' Bell whispered.

factor:0.en: Bell pointed to three overlapping circles she had drawn on the chart. Wind speed, ocean temperature, and the strange pull of the floating islands above were each a *factor* in the storm's path. Change any one of them, she said, and the whole picture shifted. We had changed none.
factor:0.cnHint: 小铃解释说三个____共同决定了风暴的走向。
factor:0.hook: A fourth circle, drawn in different ink, had no label at all.
factor:0.line: 'Island gravity is the hidden *factor* everyone forgets,' Bell told us.

condition:0.en: Old Helm checked the barometer twice, then shook his head. The *condition* of the air outside was unlike anything he had logged in thirty years at sea — pressure falling, temperature rising, and yet no rain yet. He called it a false calm. I called it frightening. Bell called it interesting.
condition:0.cnHint: 老船长检查气压表后说，外面的天气____十分异常。
condition:0.hook: The barometer needle moved again, and this time it moved fast.
condition:0.line: 'A vessel can survive this *condition*, but only if we move now,' Old Helm said.

effort:0.en: We spent an hour trying to pin the loose charts to the walls before each gust tore them free again. After the fifth *effort* Bell laughed, rolled every chart into a tight tube, and tucked them under her arm. 'The storm wins the walls,' she said. 'We keep the maps.'
effort:0.cnHint: 在经历了多次____之后，小铃找到了保护地图的好办法。
effort:0.hook: The tightest tube held a chart none of us had unrolled yet.
effort:0.line: 'One more *effort* and we get the anchor line secured,' Old Helm urged.

education:0.en: Inside the chart room, Old Helm spread a worn map across the table. 'Every island we visit adds to your *education*,' he said, tapping a blank space where our next destination should be. I traced the empty patch with one finger, already feeling that something important was about to fill it.
education:0.cnHint: 在航图室里，老舵手告诉我，每次岛屿探访都是一种____。
education:0.hook: The blank space on the map suddenly began to glow.
education:0.line: 'Every journey we take is part of your *education*, new one.'

scientist:0.en: Bell had filled the chart room with small glass jars, each holding a pinch of glowing dust from a different island. 'I work like a *scientist*,' she said proudly, holding one jar to the lamp. The dust spun inside, forming the rough shape of a mountain none of us had ever seen.
scientist:0.cnHint: 小铃像____一样，把各岛收集的发光尘埃整理成地图线索。
scientist:0.hook: The dust mountain pointed toward a gap in our charts.
scientist:0.line: 'A good *scientist* never throws away a single grain of island dust.'

physical:0.en: The storm had shaken every shelf in the chart room, and Old Helm checked each map for *physical* damage with careful hands. A torn corner caught his eye — beneath the tear was a faint second map, older and stranger. I held my breath as he peeled the two layers apart.
physical:0.cnHint: 暴风雨后，老舵手检查地图有无____损坏，却意外发现了藏在下面的旧图。
physical:0.hook: The hidden map showed an island shaped like a sleeping giant.
physical:0.line: 'Check every *physical* corner — damage hides secrets here.'

quality:0.en: Silverfang dropped a small stone on the chart table. 'Feel it,' he said. I picked it up; it was warm, lighter than it looked, and hummed faintly. 'Island stones have *quality* you can only learn by touch,' he added. Old Helm nodded and pressed the stone to the nearest blank space on the map.
quality:0.cnHint: 竞争船长让我感受岛石的____，那种触感成为地图上新坐标的线索。
quality:0.hook: Where the stone touched the map, ink began to appear.
quality:0.line: 'The *quality* of this stone tells me exactly which island made it.'

habit:0.en: Every evening in the chart room, Bell had a *habit* of reading the map aloud, island by island, like a quiet song. I started listening on my third night with the troupe, and by the fifth I was mouthing the names along with her. Old Helm smiled from the doorway without saying a word.
habit:0.cnHint: 小铃每晚都有大声朗读地图的____，我渐渐也跟着一起念了。
habit:0.hook: One name she read aloud made the lamp flicker twice.
habit:0.line: 'It is a good *habit* — the map remembers you when you say its names.'

sound:0.en: Late in the chart room, I heard a low, steady *sound* coming from inside the rolled-up maps on the shelf. Bell pressed her ear to one and smiled. 'That is the island calling,' she whispered, pulling it open on the table. A small dot near the edge pulsed like a heartbeat.
sound:0.cnHint: 航图室里，我们从卷起的地图中听到了奇怪的____，原来是某座岛屿在呼唤我们。
sound:0.hook: The pulsing dot was not on any list we had.
sound:0.line: 'Follow that *sound* — islands only call when they are ready for us.'

average:0.en: Old Helm pointed to a row of numbers along the map's edge. 'The *average* wind across these islands runs northeast,' he said, drawing a slow line with his finger. 'But this corridor here runs the wrong way.' He tapped a narrow gap between two islands, and I felt the air in the room shift, as if the map itself was breathing.
average:0.cnHint: 老舵手解释地图边缘的数据：这片区域的____风向朝东北，但有一条航道例外。
average:0.hook: That wrong-way corridor was the only path to the next word.
average:0.line: 'The *average* tells you where most ships go — not where we go.'

body:0.en: Bell unrolled the largest map in the chart room, and for the first time I saw the full *body* of the island chain laid out together, dozens of floating land masses linked by dotted paths. It looked alive, like a creature resting among the stars. Old Helm handed me a pen and said, 'Add your first mark.'
body:0.cnHint: 小铃展开最大的地图，整片浮岛群的____轮廓第一次完整地呈现在我眼前。
body:0.hook: My hand trembled as the pen touched the map.
body:0.line: 'See the whole *body* of the chain before you choose where we land.'

personal:0.en: Old Helm kept a small wooden box under his bunk. Tonight he opened it, and I saw letters, a pressed flower, and a tiny map drawn in faded ink. 'These are *personal* things,' he said softly, 'but you are part of this troupe now, so I will share one secret.' He handed me the map.
personal:0.cnHint: 老舵手打开了他的私人木盒，决定向我透露一个____的秘密。
personal:0.hook: The map showed an island none of us had ever named.
personal:0.line: 'These are *personal* things, but you have earned the right to see.'

rather:0.en: Bell spread the night charts across the table. Outside, the storm pressed hard against the glass. I expected fear, but the cabin felt *rather* warm and bright, full of the smell of tea and old paper. 'A good storm,' Bell said with a smile, 'keeps the sky honest.'
rather:0.cnHint: 风暴来袭，但船舱内却____温暖，小铃平静地研究着星图。
rather:0.hook: Then the lantern flickered, and one chart began to glow.
rather:0.line: 'It is *rather* cosy in here when the wind howls outside, yes?'

instead:0.en: Silverfang arrived soaking wet and slapped a new word-fragment on the table. We all expected him to boast. *Instead*, he sat down quietly, wrapped both hands around a cup of tea, and stared at the fragment for a long time. 'This one cost me,' was all he said.
instead:0.cnHint: 银牙回来后，大家以为他会炫耀，他____沉默地坐下，盯着新碎片。
instead:0.hook: The fragment pulsed once, then went cold and still.
instead:0.line: 'I thought about arguing, but I chose silence *instead*.'

performance:0.en: Old Helm asked each of us to read the new word aloud. Bell read it like a poem. Silverfang growled it like a challenge. When my turn came, Old Helm nodded at my *performance* and said, 'Good — the word heard you back.' The fragment shone for just a moment.
performance:0.cnHint: 老舵手让每个人朗读新单词，他对我的____表现点头称赞。
performance:0.hook: A thin line of light traced itself across the ceiling toward the door.
performance:0.line: 'Your *performance* just now told the word you were ready.'

percent:0.en: Bell tapped the cracked pressure dial above the door. 'We are at forty *percent* power,' she said calmly. 'Enough to stay warm and keep the lights on, not enough to move.' Old Helm looked at the word-fragment on the table and smiled. 'Then we study until the storm passes.'
percent:0.cnHint: 小铃报告船只只剩四十____的动力，船队只能待在原地等待风暴过去。
percent:0.hook: A second dial, one nobody had noticed before, slowly began to rise.
percent:0.line: 'Forty *percent* is enough — we have tea, light, and a good word to learn.'

achieve:0.en: I asked Old Helm how he had collected so many word-fragments over the years. He was quiet for a moment. 'You do not *achieve* a word by force,' he said, setting down his cup. 'You listen, you wait, and one morning it simply trusts you enough to stay.' I wrote that down.
achieve:0.cnHint: 老舵手告诉我，要____收集到一个词语碎片，靠的不是强求而是耐心。
achieve:0.hook: Outside, something tapped softly against the porthole glass.
achieve:0.line: 'To *achieve* a word, you must first let the word decide.'

challenge:0.en: Silverfang dropped into a chair across from me and raised an eyebrow. 'I *challenge* you,' he said lightly, pushing a blank card toward me, 'to write down what you think this fragment means before Bell explains it.' I picked up the pencil. The whole cabin leaned in to watch.
challenge:0.cnHint: 银牙向我发出____，要我在小铃解释之前，自己猜出碎片的含义。
challenge:0.hook: My pencil stopped — the word on the card was already changing.
challenge:0.line: 'I *challenge* you to guess its meaning before the storm ends.'

power:0.en: The storm cut all outside light, and the cabin ran only on its small stored *power*. In the warm dimness Old Helm held the word-fragment up, and it glowed brighter than any lantern. Bell laughed softly. 'Look at that,' she whispered. 'The word is its own light source.'
power:0.cnHint: 风暴切断了外部电源，只剩船舱微弱的____维持运转，但词语碎片自己发出了光。
power:0.hook: The glow spread to the walls, and new shapes began to appear.
power:0.line: 'When outside *power* fails, a good word lights the way instead.'

key:0.en: The storm had locked every chest in the map room. Old Helm knelt before the largest one and lifted a small iron object from his coat pocket. 'This,' he said quietly, 'is the *key* to the next island.' The whole troupe held its breath as the lock turned with a soft click.
key:0.cnHint: 老舵手从口袋里取出一样东西，说它是前往下一座岛屿的____。
key:0.hook: The chest creaked open, and something inside glowed.
key:0.line: 'This little iron piece is the *key* to everything we have searched for.'

issue:0.en: Rain hammered the cabin roof as Bell spread the old charts across the table. She pointed to a torn edge where two routes did not match. 'This *issue* with the maps has kept us circling the same cloud bank for two days,' she said. Old Helm nodded slowly and reached for his pen.
issue:0.cnHint: 贝尔指着地图上的矛盾之处，说这个____让我们兜圈子了两天。
issue:0.hook: Old Helm's pen stopped — there was a third route no one had drawn.
issue:0.line: 'The real *issue* is that someone removed part of this map on purpose.'

against:0.en: The cabin walls shook as wind pushed hard from outside. I leaned *against* the heavy door with both hands to hold it shut while Bell tied down the loose charts. Old Helm lit the small lamp above the table and smiled. 'Good,' he said. 'The storm tests us, and we are still here.'
against:0.cnHint: 我用身体____着舱门，不让狂风把它吹开。
against:0.hook: Something on the other side of the door knocked — twice, then once.
against:0.line: 'Put your back *against* the door and hold it until I say stop.'

matter:0.en: Bell found me sitting alone near the cold stove, staring at nothing. 'What is the *matter*?' she asked, pulling a stool close. I told her the word I had collected today felt wrong, like a piece that did not fit any puzzle. She took it from my hand and held it to the lamp light.
matter:0.cnHint: 贝尔看出我神情不对，问我是怎么了——"有什么____吗？"
matter:0.hook: The word glowed a colour none of us had ever seen before.
matter:0.line: 'Tell me what is the *matter* — we share every trouble on this ship.'

raise:0.en: Old Helm stood at the centre of the cabin and looked at each of us in turn. 'We need more lantern oil to cross the storm belt,' he said. 'I will *raise* the funds by trading our spare word-maps at the next dock.' Bell wrote the number down carefully. The plan felt thin but possible.
raise:0.cnHint: 老舵手说他要用备用词图来____资金，购买穿越风暴带所需的灯油。
raise:0.hook: Silverfang's ship had already reached that dock, and the oil was almost gone.
raise:0.line: 'I will *raise* enough coins to keep every lantern burning through the storm.'

option:0.en: The storm blocked the northern pass and a thick fog covered the southern one. Old Helm drew two small crosses on the chart and then looked up. 'There is no good *option* here,' he admitted, 'only a less dangerous one.' The crew went quiet. Outside, lightning lit the windows in short white flashes.
option:0.cnHint: 两条航路都很危险，老舵手坦言没有好的____，只有相对安全的那个。
option:0.hook: Then Bell noticed a third cross, already drawn in someone else's ink.
option:0.line: 'Every *option* carries a cost — choose the one you can live with.'

society:0.en: Bell had collected a word that opened a small door inside the cabin wall. Beyond it was a tiny reading room, lined with old books. A note on the first page said the room had belonged to a travelling *society* of word-seekers long before our troupe existed. Old Helm touched the books with great care.
society:0.cnHint: 暗门后的小书房曾属于一个词语探索者的____，早于我们的团队存在。
society:0.hook: The last book had our names written inside, and no page was blank.
society:0.line: 'This *society* of word-seekers walked the same sky roads before us.'

whole:0.en: We spread every collected word across the cabin floor, end to end, until they covered the boards like a strange bright carpet. Old Helm stepped back and looked at them together. 'The *whole* set forms one map,' he said softly. I had never seen him smile that wide. Bell began to copy the shape into her chart.
whole:0.cnHint: 老舵手把所有词语拼在一起，发现____组合恰好构成一张完整的地图。
whole:0.hook: At the map's centre was an island none of our charts had ever named.
whole:0.line: 'The *whole* collection was always meant to be read as a single map.'

receive:0.en: Inside the map room, Bell spread a tangle of old charts across the table. A message tube clattered through the brass pipe in the wall. 'We *receive* a signal from the storm zone,' she said, pressing the rolled paper to the lamp. Strange symbols glowed along its edge.
receive:0.cnHint: 小铃在地图室里从传信管____了一份来自风暴海域的神秘信号。
receive:0.hook: The symbols matched no island we had ever found.
receive:0.line: 'We *receive* a signal — and I don't like what it says.'

encourage:0.en: Old Helm gathered us around the iron stove while rain hammered the hull. My hands would not stop shaking. He looked at me steadily and said, 'Fear is normal. Let it pass through you.' His calm voice seemed to *encourage* every person in the room, not just me.
encourage:0.cnHint: 面对风暴的恐惧，老船长用平静的话语____了大家。
encourage:0.hook: Then a second sound rose beneath the rain — something vast and breathing.
encourage:0.line: 'I *encourage* you to be afraid — it means you are still thinking.'

travel:0.en: Bell traced a glowing line across the chart with her fingertip. 'Our *travel* through the storm zone must follow this narrow current,' she explained. 'Stray one degree and the wind will spin us off the edge.' We all stared at how thin that safe line was.
travel:0.cnHint: 小铃在图表上画出穿越风暴海域____的唯一安全路线。
travel:0.hook: The line was barely wider than a finger.
travel:0.line: 'Safe *travel* through the storm means trusting a line this thin.'

strong:0.en: Old Helm knocked on the inner wall with his knuckle. The deep ring it gave back made him smile. 'She is *strong*,' he said, meaning the ship. 'Builders packed three layers of sky-oak into every plank.' I pressed my palm against the wood and felt it hum with solidity.
strong:0.cnHint: 老船长检查船壁，确认这艘船足够____，能够穿越风暴。
strong:0.hook: Outside, the first true gust arrived and the whole frame groaned.
strong:0.line: 'She is *strong* — three layers of sky-oak, every plank.'

chance:0.en: Silverfang's voice crackled through the speaking-tube, sharp with urgency. 'There is one *chance* to cross before the eye of the storm closes,' she said. 'We move in ten minutes or we wait three days.' Old Helm looked at the crew. Nobody spoke. Slowly, every hand went up.
chance:0.cnHint: 银牙通过传话筒告知众人，穿越风暴只有一次____。
chance:0.hook: Ten minutes felt like ten seconds.
chance:0.line: 'One *chance*, ten minutes — after that the door shuts forever.'

solve:0.en: The navigation lamp flickered and Bell dropped to her knees beside the base, her tools already out. 'I can *solve* this,' she said quietly, more to herself than to us. The storm outside seemed to press against the glass, waiting. Three minutes later, the lamp blazed steady and gold.
solve:0.cnHint: 导航灯突然熄灭，小铃镇定地说自己能____这个问题。
solve:0.hook: Steady gold light meant we had a heading — for now.
solve:0.line: 'Give me three minutes. I can *solve* this with my eyes shut.'

quite:0.en: I expected the map room to feel safe, tucked deep inside the ship. It was *quite* the opposite. Every groan of the hull was louder here, every shift in the current more visible on the swinging charts. Old Helm poured tea anyway and handed me a cup without a word.
quite:0.cnHint: 我以为地图室会让人感到安心，结果情况____相反。
quite:0.hook: The tea was warm, but my fingers refused to believe it.
quite:0.line: 'It is *quite* the opposite of safe in here — and that is fine.'

technology:0.en: Bell pointed to a small brass device bolted above the chart table. 'This is island *technology*, not ours,' she said. 'The builders of the floating islands left it. It reads storm currents the way we read words.' She touched a dial and a soft chime filled the room like a question.
technology:0.cnHint: 小铃向大家介绍固定在桌上方的那台神秘装置，称其为浮岛建造者留下的____。
technology:0.hook: The chime faded, but the dial kept turning on its own.
technology:0.line: 'This *technology* reads storms the way we read words — trust it.'

nearly:0.en: The storm had kept us below deck for two days. Our little cabin smelled of salt and wet rope. Old Helm sat by the lantern, counting our word-fragments on the table. 'We have *nearly* enough,' he said, spreading seven glowing pieces across the wood. One more, and the next island would appear on our map.
nearly:0.cnHint: 暴风雨把大家困在船舱里，团长数着地图碎片，发现____凑齐了所有碎片。
nearly:0.hook: But the eighth fragment slipped through a crack in the floor.
nearly:0.line: 'We have *nearly* enough pieces to unlock the next island.'

wrong:0.en: Bell spread the word-fragments on the cabin table and began to arrange them. The pattern looked clean at first, but the map that formed showed ocean where land should be. 'Something is *wrong*,' Bell said, frowning at the shape. I leaned in and spotted it: one fragment was flipped upside down.
wrong:0.cnHint: 小铃在船舱里拼地图碎片，却发现拼出来的图形有些____，其中一块碎片放反了。
wrong:0.hook: Beneath the flipped fragment, faint new letters began to glow.
wrong:0.line: 'Something is *wrong* with the way this fragment is placed.'

variety:0.en: Old Helm kept a small chest under his bunk. After the storm locked us inside, he opened it for the first time. Inside was a *variety* of word-fragments: some carved on bone, some pressed into wax, some written in light. I had no idea one chest could hold so many different kinds.
variety:0.cnHint: 团长在船舱里打开了一个宝箱，里面装有各种各样____的地图碎片，让众人大开眼界。
variety:0.hook: One fragment pulsed orange, unlike all the rest.
variety:0.line: 'This chest holds a *variety* of fragments I have collected over the years.'

clear:0.en: The porthole was fogged from our breath, and the storm outside made everything grey. Bell wiped the glass slowly. Suddenly the mist lifted for just a moment, and the sky outside was *clear*: sharp stars, still air, and the outline of a distant island hanging like a lantern above the clouds.
clear:0.cnHint: 小铃擦净舷窗玻璃，暴风雨突然短暂停歇，窗外的天空变得____，远处一座岛屿清晰可见。
clear:0.hook: The island vanished again before anyone else could look.
clear:0.line: 'Look — the sky is finally *clear* and I can see the next island.'

gain:0.en: We had been stuck in the storm for so long that Old Helm decided to use the time well. He taught me how to read the glow on each word-fragment. By the time the wind died down, I could tell a sea-word from a sky-word by touch alone. The *gain* felt bigger than any island we had found.
gain:0.cnHint: 被困船舱的时间里，团长教了我辨认碎片的方法，这份____比找到任何一座新岛都更珍贵。
gain:0.hook: Old Helm smiled and pressed the hardest fragment into my hand.
gain:0.line: 'The *gain* from one quiet storm can last you a lifetime of sailing.'

huge:0.en: Old Helm unrolled the largest chart we owned and pinned it to the cabin wall. I had seen it folded many times, but open it was *huge*, nearly covering the entire wall from floor to ceiling. Dozens of islands were marked on it, and most of them had no names yet. My fingers itched to explore every one.
huge:0.cnHint: 团长在船舱里展开一张地图，摊开后____无比，上面密密麻麻标注着许多还没有名字的岛屿。
huge:0.hook: One unmarked island in the corner seemed to glow faintly on its own.
huge:0.line: 'This chart is *huge* — and most of these islands are still waiting for names.'

diet:0.en: Silverfang arrived at our cabin door with a bowl of something warm. 'Storm rations,' he said with a small shrug. 'Plain *diet*, I know.' It was just rice and dried seaweed, but he had arranged it carefully, and a word-fragment sat on the rim of the bowl like a little gift, glowing soft blue.
diet:0.cnHint: 银牙端来简单的暴风雨口粮，这种____虽朴素，碗沿上却放着一块泛着蓝光的地图碎片。
diet:0.hook: The word glowing on the fragment was the name of our next island.
diet:0.line: 'Plain *diet* it may be, but I hid a little surprise on the rim of your bowl.'

traditional:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a long cloth covered in hand-drawn routes. 'Every *traditional* path between islands is marked here,' he said, tracing a line with one finger. The cloth smelled of old wood and rain. I leaned closer, trying to read the tiny words stitched along each route. One word glowed faintly gold.
traditional:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室向我展示了记录____航线的古老布图。
traditional:0.hook: The golden word on the cloth began to move.
traditional:0.line: 'Every *traditional* path between islands is marked here.'

expert:0.en: Bell spread the star charts across the low table and studied them without blinking. 'She is the only *expert* in reading storm-born light,' Old Helm told me quietly. I watched her draw a small circle on the chart, then another, connecting them with a single careful line. The circles formed a word.
expert:0.cnHint: 小铃是阅读风暴之光的____，她在星图上画出了一个神秘的词语。
expert:0.hook: The word she drew matched nothing on our current map.
expert:0.line: 'Bell is the only *expert* in reading storm-born light on this sea.'

heart:0.en: The lantern at the center of the cabin was called the *heart* of the ship by everyone in the troupe. As long as it burned, Bell said, the islands would stay on the map. Tonight it flickered. I cupped my hands around it and felt a word form under my palms, warm and steady as a pulse.
heart:0.cnHint: 船舱中央的灯笼是船的____，今晚它开始闪烁，而我的双掌感知到了一个词语。
heart:0.hook: Bell whispered that no heart had flickered twice and survived.
heart:0.line: 'As long as the *heart* of the ship burns, we stay on the map.'

mind:0.en: Rain lashed the porthole as Old Helm spread the new map fragment across the table. 'Every island we have found so far fits together like a puzzle,' he said. I watched his *mind* work through the pattern, connections forming faster than I could follow. Outside, thunder rolled across the dark water.
mind:0.cnHint: 老船长的____飞速运转，试图拼出风暴海域的地图碎片。
mind:0.hook: One piece of the map was still missing — and the storm was closing in.
mind:0.line: 'A sharp *mind* sees the pattern before the map is even finished.'

rise:0.en: Bell pressed her ear to the hull and frowned. 'Water,' she said quietly. I looked at the gauge on the wall — the number showed a slow, steady *rise* that none of us wanted to see. Old Helm ordered everyone to their stations without raising his voice, which somehow made it more frightening.
rise:0.cnHint: 船舱里水位的____让所有人意识到危险正在逼近。
rise:0.hook: The gauge kept climbing, and the nearest island was still an hour away.
rise:0.line: 'A *rise* like this means we patch the hull right now, not later.'

prove:0.en: Silverfang arrived soaking wet, a rolled chart under one arm. 'I told you the eastern current would shift,' she said. Old Helm crossed his arms. 'Then *prove* it.' She unrolled the chart on the deck and pointed to three red marks that lined up perfectly with our current drift. No one argued after that.
prove:0.cnHint: 银牙船长要用一张航图____自己的判断是正确的。
prove:0.hook: If she was right, our planned route was already useless.
prove:0.line: 'I will *prove* my reading is correct — give me one minute.'

associate:0.en: Bell introduced a wiry woman who had slipped aboard during the chaos of the storm. 'She is my *associate*,' Bell said simply. The stranger set a small box of tools on the table and nodded. Old Helm studied her for a moment, then gave a short nod back — his way of saying she was welcome.
associate:0.cnHint: 贝尔带来了一位____，这位新面孔悄悄登上了船。
associate:0.hook: No one had asked yet what was inside that small box of tools.
associate:0.line: 'My *associate* knows this part of the sky better than anyone alive.'

message:0.en: A folded slip of paper dropped through the vent above the stove. Bell picked it up, read it twice, and said nothing for a long moment. 'What does it say?' I asked. She smoothed the paper flat so we could all see — the *message* was only four words, but those four words changed everything about our plan.
message:0.cnHint: 一张纸条悄然落下，上面的____让整个队伍改变了计划。
message:0.hook: Four words — and Old Helm's expression shifted from calm to urgent.
message:0.line: 'This *message* did not come from any island we have visited.'

development:0.en: Old Helm pinned the newest map fragment beside the others and stood back. 'Look at the *development* of the route,' he said, tracing the chain of islands with one finger. Each one had unlocked the next, like a sentence writing itself across the sky. I felt a quiet thrill — we were not wandering; we were following something.
development:0.cnHint: 老船长指着地图，分析整条路线的____规律。
development:0.hook: The pattern pointed toward a region none of our charts had ever named.
development:0.line: 'The *development* of this route is too careful to be an accident.'

later:0.en: The leak was patched, the storm had softened to a drizzle, and someone had made a pot of something warm that smelled of cinnamon. '*Later*,' said Old Helm, settling into his chair, 'we will laugh about tonight.' I was not sure I believed him yet, but the warmth in his voice made the cabin feel a little larger.
later:0.cnHint: 风暴平息后，老船长说____我们会把今晚当作笑话来回忆。
later:0.hook: But the night was not quite finished with us yet.
later:0.line: '*Later*, when we are safe, I will tell you what I was truly thinking.'

maintain:0.en: Bell worked silently at the navigation desk, adjusting small brass dials with careful fingers. 'She does that every night,' Old Helm told me softly. 'It is how she can *maintain* our heading even when the stars are hidden.' I watched her finish, cap her pen, and look up with the quiet confidence of someone who never doubts her own work.
maintain:0.cnHint: 贝尔每晚调试仪器，以____准确的航向。
maintain:0.hook: Tonight, with the clouds thickening, her ritual mattered more than ever.
maintain:0.line: 'We *maintain* our course by trust as much as by instruments.'

action:0.en: Rain lashed the wooden walls of our shelter on Storm Shelf island. Bell spread the map on the floor and traced the swirling routes with one finger. 'We cannot wait,' she said firmly. Old Helm nodded. Every *action* we took now would decide whether the troupe reached the calm waters beyond the clouds.
action:0.cnHint: 贝尔在庇护所里摊开地图，老舵要大家立刻采取____，不能再等待。
action:0.hook: Outside, the ropes snapped — something large had arrived.
action:0.line: 'Every *action* counts when the storm is this close.'

program:0.en: Inside the shelter, Old Helm pinned a sheet of paper to the wall. It listed each step of our crossing in careful order. 'This is our *program* for tomorrow,' he said, tapping each line with his pen. Bell and I studied it in silence while thunder rolled across the shelf outside.
program:0.cnHint: 老舵在庇护所内贴出明日渡越风暴的____，逐条向大家说明。
program:0.hook: One step on the list had been crossed out by an unknown hand.
program:0.line: 'Follow the *program* exactly, and we will all get through.'

situation:0.en: Water crept under the shelter door and spread across the floor in a thin, cold sheet. Bell climbed onto a crate and looked out through the high window. She turned back to us, her face serious. 'The *situation* outside is worse than I thought,' she said. Old Helm pulled his coat tighter and said nothing.
situation:0.cnHint: 贝尔从高窗望出去，发现外面的____比预想的更加严峻。
situation:0.hook: Then the shelter's single lantern flickered and went out.
situation:0.line: 'The *situation* is bad, but we have faced worse together.'

order:0.en: Old Helm lined up our supplies along the wall: rope, dried fruit, lantern oil, and three small word-fragments wrapped in cloth. He checked each item twice. 'There is an *order* to packing for a storm crossing,' he told me quietly, 'and breaking that order costs lives.' I began to understand why the troupe trusted him.
order:0.cnHint: 老舵按照严格的____整理物资，告诉我打乱这个____可能很危险。
order:0.hook: The last bundle felt heavier than it should have.
order:0.line: 'There is an *order* to things — learn it before we sail.'

event:0.en: Bell pulled out a small logbook and opened it to a worn page. 'Three years ago, on a night like this, something changed everything for us,' she said softly. Old Helm stared at the ceiling. That *event* had left a blank space in the log that nobody had ever filled in. I did not ask — not yet.
event:0.cnHint: 贝尔翻开航海日志，提到三年前改变了船队命运的一个____。
event:0.hook: The blank page was not entirely blank after all.
event:0.line: 'That *event* is why we never cross Storm Shelf before dawn.'

account:0.en: I found a folded note tucked inside the shelter's old stove. It was a rough written *account* of a previous crossing — wind speeds, island positions, a narrow escape from a whirlpool. The handwriting matched no one in our troupe. Bell read it over my shoulder and whispered, 'Whoever wrote this survived. That is enough.'
account:0.cnHint: 我在炉子里发现了一份前人留下的____，详细记录了上次渡越的经历。
account:0.hook: The note ended mid-sentence, as if the writer had left in a hurry.
account:0.line: 'This *account* may be the most useful thing we have found all year.'

deal:0.en: Old Helm spread his hands on the table and looked at Silverfang, who had appeared at our shelter door soaking wet. 'You want safe passage through my route. I want the eastern word-fragment,' Old Helm said. 'That is a fair *deal*.' Silverfang shook water from her coat, thought for a moment, then slowly nodded.
deal:0.cnHint: 老舵和银牙在庇护所里谈条件，达成了一笔互利的____。
deal:0.hook: Silverfang's smile did not quite reach her eyes.
deal:0.line: 'A *deal* like this only works if both sides keep their word.'

within:0.en: The storm had kept us below deck for two days. Old Helm spread a new map across the table and tapped a glowing circle at its centre. 'Everything we need is *within* this ring,' he said. The circle was small — just three islands — but each one pulsed like a held breath.
within:0.cnHint: 暴风雨期间，老舵手在船舱内展开地图，指出所有目标都在____一个小圈子里。
within:0.hook: But the smallest island had no name, only a question mark.
within:0.line: 'Everything we need is *within* this ring,' Old Helm said, his finger steady on the map.

either:0.en: Bell held up two old keys she had found under the floorboards. One was iron, one was brass. 'I have tested *either* key in the lock,' she said, 'and neither one turns.' Old Helm frowned. Somewhere above us, thunder rolled like a slow warning, and the ship groaned.
either:0.cnHint: 小铃找到两把钥匙，但____一把都打不开那把锁。
either:0.hook: Then we noticed the lock itself was upside down.
either:0.line: 'I have tested *either* key, and neither one turns,' Bell said quietly.

various:0.en: Old Helm kept a wooden chest under his bunk. Tonight he opened it and showed me *various* tools inside — compasses, folded charts, small glass jars full of coloured sand from islands we had never visited. Each object was a memory. I felt the weight of all those journeys at once.
various:0.cnHint: 老舵手打开箱子，向我展示里面____各式各样的航海工具和纪念品。
various:0.hook: One jar held sand that shimmered like a living star.
various:0.line: 'These *various* tools each saved us once,' Old Helm said, lifting a small brass compass.

main:0.en: Silverfang arrived at our cabin door with a rolled chart under one arm. He pointed to a wide channel on the map. 'The *main* route through the storm is here,' he said, dragging his finger along a bold line. 'Dangerous, but fast.' Old Helm studied it and said nothing for a long time.
main:0.cnHint: 银牙指着地图上的____主航道，说那是穿越风暴最快的路线。
main:0.hook: The bold line ended just before a blank space on the map.
main:0.line: 'The *main* route is here — dangerous, but it leads through,' Silverfang said firmly.

employee:0.en: A thin man knocked on the cabin door during the storm. He said he was an *employee* of the island harbour master, sent to warn us about rocks hidden below the waves. His coat was soaked and his hands shook, but his eyes were calm. Old Helm handed him a warm cup and listened.
employee:0.cnHint: 暴风雨中，一名港务长的____雇员冒雨赶来，提醒我们水下有暗礁。
employee:0.hook: He left before we could ask which harbour he came from.
employee:0.line: 'I am an *employee* of the harbour master — I came to warn you,' the man said.

class:0.en: Bell gathered us around the small table and laid out six word-fragments, each on a separate piece of bark. 'Every word belongs to a *class*,' she explained, sorting them into two neat rows. 'Knowing the class tells you where the word fits on a map.' It was the most useful lesson I had heard.
class:0.cnHint: 小铃在船舱里给大家上课，说明每个词都有其____种类，决定它在地图上的位置。
class:0.hook: One bark piece trembled and slid toward the lantern on its own.
class:0.line: 'Every word belongs to a *class*, and the class shows where it leads,' Bell said.

behavior:0.en: The ship's navigation lamp had been acting strangely all evening — flickering twice, then going steady, then flickering again. Old Helm watched it with narrowed eyes. 'That *behavior* means a charged cloud is close,' he said. He was not worried, only careful. We all moved a little away from the metal railing.
behavior:0.cnHint: 船上的导航灯出现异常____举止，老舵长判断附近有带电云层。
behavior:0.hook: Then the lamp flashed three times and went completely dark.
behavior:0.line: 'That *behavior* from the lamp means a charged cloud is near,' Old Helm warned.

disease:0.en: Among Old Helm's charts was one marked with red dots. 'Each dot is an island we cannot land on,' Bell told me softly. 'A *disease* swept through years ago — the trees are still grey.' She did not seem sad, only respectful, the way you feel standing before something larger than yourself.
disease:0.cnHint: 地图上的红点标记着曾被____疾病侵袭、至今无法登陆的岛屿。
disease:0.hook: One red dot sat exactly where our next word was supposed to be.
disease:0.line: 'A *disease* took those islands long ago — we honour them by passing carefully,' Bell said.

worker:0.en: The rain hammered the hull all night. By morning, Old Helm had mapped every leak. 'Each of us is a *worker* in this troupe,' he said, handing me a bucket and a grin. I bailed water until my arms burned, but the ship held. When the clouds finally broke, a new island glittered on the horizon.
worker:0.cnHint: 暴雨之夜，老舵手让每个人都成为船上的____，我们一起奋力排水，守住了飞船。
worker:0.hook: But something else had come aboard with the storm.
worker:0.line: 'Every *worker* on this ship earns their place — no exceptions.'

control:0.en: The storm tossed our ship like a leaf. Bell gripped the navigation wheel and closed her eyes. 'I have to *control* my breathing first,' she murmured, 'then I can steer.' One steady breath at a time, she brought us level. The wild sky smoothed into a river of stars above our heads.
control:0.cnHint: 狂风中，领航员用____呼吸的方式稳住了自己，最终将飞船带出了险境。
control:0.hook: Then the compass spun — and pointed somewhere it had never pointed before.
control:0.line: 'If you can *control* your fear, you can steer through anything.'

product:0.en: Old Helm spread a jar of glowing paste on the cracked mast. 'Storm-seal,' he said proudly. 'A *product* of three islands and twenty bad ideas.' I laughed, but the paste held. By dawn the mast stood straight and the word 'product' glowed faintly on our map — a new fragment unlocked.
product:0.cnHint: 老舵手用一种由多个岛屿材料制成的特殊____修好了断裂的桅杆，地图上随即亮起了新的碎片。
product:0.hook: The sealed mast began to hum — very softly, very strangely.
product:0.line: 'This paste is the *product* of every mistake I ever made at sea.'

practice:0.en: Bell made me trace star-paths on the chart for an hour. 'Why so many times?' I asked. 'Because *practice* is how a guess becomes a skill,' she said simply. By the tenth try my lines were clean and true. That night I found our position without help, and the whole troupe cheered around the warm lamp.
practice:0.cnHint: 领航员让我反复描绘星图，告诉我____是将猜测变为技能的唯一方式。
practice:0.hook: My final line pointed straight at an island no chart had ever named.
practice:0.line: '*Practice* every night — the stars don't wait for you to feel ready.'

environment:0.en: The storm corridor smelled of salt and burnt cloud. Old Helm called it a harsh *environment*, but said every hard place teaches something softer places cannot. I watched sparks of lightning paint the walls of our cabin gold. When we flew clear, I understood — beauty lives inside the difficult things too.
environment:0.cnHint: 老舵手说，恶劣的____本身就是一位老师，我在闪电中慢慢明白了他的话。
environment:0.hook: Ahead, the air turned a colour none of us could name.
environment:0.line: 'A tough *environment* sharpens you faster than any calm island ever could.'

system:0.en: Silverfang docked beside us in the storm's eye and tossed over a rolled-up chart. 'My crew built a *system* for reading wind tunnels,' she called out. 'Use it.' I unrolled it — neat arrows, clear symbols. With her system we cut an hour off our path and reached shelter before the second wave hit.
system:0.cnHint: 竞争船长向我们分享了一套读取风向隧道的____，帮助我们提前抵达了安全地带。
system:0.hook: Silverfang's parting smile hid something she hadn't told us yet.
system:0.line: 'Our *system* isn't perfect, but it's kept my crew alive every time.'

natural:0.en: I was shaking as we flew into the gale. Bell put a hand on my shoulder. 'Being scared is *natural*,' she said. 'It means you understand the risk.' That small sentence settled something inside me. I took my post, watched the stars through the rain, and found I could think clearly after all.
natural:0.cnHint: 领航员告诉我，感到害怕是____的，这句话让我在风暴中找回了冷静。
natural:0.hook: Then a shape moved beneath the clouds — too large to be a bird.
natural:0.line: 'Fear is *natural* — what matters is what you do with it next.'

free:0.en: The storm broke near dawn. Old Helm cut the safety ropes himself and laughed. 'We're *free*!' he shouted into the open sky. Bell cheered. Even Silverfang, watching from a distance, raised one hand. I breathed in the clean air and felt the word settle on the map like a warm light.
free:0.cnHint: 风暴结束后，老舵手剪断了安全绳，大声宣告我们终于____了，地图上随即亮起了温暖的光。
free:0.hook: The new light on the map pointed toward an island that moved.
free:0.line: 'When the storm lets go, we are finally *free* to choose our own course.'

receive:1.en: A sealed bottle tumbled onto the deck from the grey clouds above. Old Helm caught it with both hands and held it up to the pale light. Inside was a rolled paper — a message we did not expect to *receive* in the middle of a storm-dark sky.
receive:1.cnHint: 一只漂流瓶从云层中落下，老舵从瓶中____了一张神秘纸条。
receive:1.hook: The handwriting on the note matched no one aboard.
receive:1.line: 'We *receive* this message as a warning, not a gift.'

encourage:1.en: The wind howled and our small vessel shook hard. Bell gripped the railing, face pale, ready to turn back. Old Helm placed a steady hand on her shoulder and spoke quietly. His words were enough to *encourage* her to take the wheel again and face the dark clouds ahead.
encourage:1.cnHint: 风暴中贝尔几乎放弃，老舵的话____了她重新掌舵。
encourage:1.hook: The clouds parted just enough to reveal something enormous.
encourage:1.line: 'Let the storm *encourage* you — it means we are close.'

travel:1.en: No island stays still in this part of the sky. The floating rocks *travel* with the wind, drifting east by dawn and west by dusk. Bell spread her charts on the wet deck and traced their slow paths with one finger, searching for the gap we needed to pass through safely.
travel:1.cnHint: 这片海域的浮岛会随风____，贝尔正在追踪它们的轨迹。
travel:1.hook: One island was moving far faster than the charts predicted.
travel:1.line: 'Islands that *travel* this fast are hiding something beneath them.'

strong:1.en: The gust hit us broadside and the mast groaned like a tired old voice. Bell shouted that most ships would have broken apart by now. But our vessel held. Old Helm had rebuilt every joint himself — the frame was *strong* enough to laugh at weather like this, he said.
strong:1.cnHint: 狂风袭来，老舵亲手加固的船体____得令人惊叹。
strong:1.hook: Then a second gust arrived, twice as fierce as the first.
strong:1.line: 'She is *strong*, but even she has her limit — move!'

chance:1.en: A narrow gap opened between two spinning storm-walls, lasting no more than a minute. Bell saw it first and called out. Old Helm spun the wheel without hesitation. It was a small *chance*, barely wide enough for our hull, but it was the only one the sky was willing to offer.
chance:1.cnHint: 两道风墙之间出现了短暂裂缝，这是穿越风暴的唯一____。
chance:1.hook: The gap began closing before we reached the halfway point.
chance:1.line: 'One *chance* — if we miss it, we wait three days in this storm.'

solve:1.en: Rain hammered the deck and our compass spun in circles, useless. Bell knelt over her charts and muttered numbers under her breath. She had faced broken instruments before. Within minutes she managed to *solve* the problem using only the angle of the wind and the colour of the clouds above.
solve:1.cnHint: 指南针失灵，贝尔只凭风向和云色____了导航难题。
solve:1.hook: Her new heading pointed straight into the darkest part of the sky.
solve:1.line: 'I can *solve* this — just give me two minutes and some quiet.'

quite:1.en: We cleared the storm wall at last and floated into open sky. The silence was sudden and total. None of us spoke for a long moment. It was *quite* unlike anything I had felt before — not just relief, but a deep stillness, as if the sky itself had stopped to breathe with us.
quite:1.cnHint: 穿越风暴后，那份寂静____出乎所有人意料。
quite:1.hook: Then, out of that stillness, a bell rang from somewhere below.
quite:1.line: 'It is *quite* strange — the air here smells of old paper and ink.'

technology:1.en: Silverfang's vessel appeared through the last wall of rain, sleek and fast. It moved without sails, powered by spinning rings of copper that hummed in the wet air. Old Helm frowned. That kind of *technology* did not belong to any troupe we had ever encountered on the floating islands before.
technology:1.cnHint: 银牙的船使用了一种奇异____，完全不需要帆就能前行。
technology:1.hook: The copper rings began to spin faster, aimed directly at us.
technology:1.line: 'Their *technology* is unknown to me — and that is never good news.'

compare:1.en: Old Helm unrolled two worn charts on the deck rail and held them side by side. 'The storm lanes have shifted,' he said quietly. I watched him *compare* the old lines with the new ones, tracing each gap with a careful finger. Something on the second chart made him go still.
compare:1.cnHint: 老船长把两张海图摊开，仔细____，发现风暴航道已经改变。
compare:1.hook: His finger stopped — right where our route crossed the darkest mark.
compare:1.line: '*Compare* these two charts and tell me what is missing.'

past:1.en: Bell stood at the bow and looked out over the grey water without speaking. I asked her once what lay beyond the next island. She smiled, but her eyes were somewhere far away. 'Every sailor carries the *past* like extra weight,' she said softly. 'The trick is not letting it slow you down.'
past:1.cnHint: 领航员望着远处，感慨每个水手都背负着____。
past:1.hook: Then she pointed ahead — and I saw the clouds moving the wrong way.
past:1.line: 'The *past* is heavy, but we sail forward all the same.'

suffer:1.en: The wind hit us without warning, tilting the deck sharply to one side. Ropes snapped tight and barrels rolled. Old Helm gripped the mast and shouted for us to hold on. We would *suffer* no real harm if we kept our heads, he promised, but the sky above looked far from convinced.
suffer:1.cnHint: 突如其来的狂风袭击船只，老船长承诺大家不会____太多，但天色不太乐观。
suffer:1.hook: A second gust arrived, twice as strong as the first.
suffer:1.line: 'We will *suffer* no harm if everyone holds their post!'

almost:1.en: A giant wave rose on the port side, taller than the mast. Bell spun the wheel hard, and for one long breath the deck stood nearly vertical. My boots left the wood and I grabbed a rope just in time. We *almost* tipped — close enough that my heart was still hammering a minute later.
almost:1.cnHint: 一个巨浪袭来，船____就要翻了，大家都捏了一把汗。
almost:1.hook: Bell's knuckles were white, and she had not let go of the wheel.
almost:1.line: 'We *almost* lost the whole cargo just now — check every line!'

especially:1.en: After the worst of the storm passed, Old Helm walked the deck checking for damage. The eastern ropes had frayed badly, and two lanterns were gone. He tested every joint with his hands, pausing at the mast base. 'Everything needs checking after a storm,' he said, '*especially* the parts you think are fine.'
especially:1.cnHint: 风暴过后，老船长检查船体损伤，____提醒大家注意那些看似没问题的地方。
especially:1.hook: He pressed one plank and it gave a low, unhappy groan.
especially:1.line: 'Check everything carefully, *especially* the mast base — do it now.'

publish:1.en: Silverfang pulled a damp notebook from inside his coat and smoothed its pages on his knee. 'I write down every storm I sail through,' he told me with a grin. 'One day I will *publish* all of it — a guide for fools brave enough to cross this sea.' He winked, then went back to writing.
publish:1.cnHint: 竞争船长表示，他记录每一次风暴，打算有朝一日____一本航海指南。
publish:1.hook: One page near the back was sealed shut with red wax.
publish:1.line: 'I plan to *publish* this one day — if we survive long enough.'

activity:1.en: Once the clouds thinned, the floating island ahead came into view, alive with movement. Lights blinked along its edges, small boats circled its base, and voices carried across the water. Old Helm raised his looking-glass and nodded slowly. 'That much *activity* means they found something,' he said. 'We should hurry.'
activity:1.cnHint: 前方浮岛上灯火闪烁、人声嘈杂，老船长说如此多的____意味着有人发现了什么。
activity:1.hook: Through the glass I caught a flash of gold among the crowd.
activity:1.line: 'All that *activity* on the island — someone has made a discovery.'

science:1.en: Bell spread a small book open on the chart table as rain tapped the window. She explained how the pressure of air changes before a storm and how sailors could learn to read those signs. 'This is not luck,' she said, tapping the page firmly. 'It is *science*, and it can keep us alive.'
science:1.cnHint: 领航员向大家解释如何通过气压变化预判风暴，她说这不是运气，而是____。
science:1.hook: She turned the page — and showed a diagram of exactly where we were.
science:1.line: 'Trust the *science*, not your gut — the numbers do not lie.'

contribute:1.en: The storm had torn half our sail, and every hand was needed on deck. 'Each of us must *contribute* something,' Old Helm called out, his voice steady above the howling wind. I grabbed a rope without thinking. Bell was already tying knots faster than I could count.
contribute:1.cnHint: 暴风撕裂了船帆，老舵长要求每个人都____一份力量。
contribute:1.hook: But the rope in my hands began to pull — toward something below.
contribute:1.line: 'Each of us must *contribute* something, or we all go down together.'

share:1.en: When the storm finally passed, Old Helm divided the last of our dry bread on the open deck. He gave each person an equal *share*, no more and no less, even saving a piece for the lookout still up in the crow's nest. The stars came out one by one above us.
share:1.cnHint: 风暴过后，老舵长把干粮分成几份，每人得到公平的____。
share:1.hook: The lookout's piece sat untouched — and the crow's nest was empty.
share:1.line: 'Everyone gets a fair *share*, even those we cannot yet see.'

decade:1.en: Bell spread the old map flat against the mast. 'This chart is over a *decade* old,' she said quietly, tracing a faded line with one finger. The storm had pushed us far off course, into waters no one in our troupe had ever crossed. The ink here was smudged beyond reading.
decade:1.cnHint: 领航员发现海图已有____之久，无法指引我们穿越陌生水域。
decade:1.hook: Beneath the smudge, something had been deliberately scratched out.
decade:1.line: 'A map over a *decade* old has secrets the maker never meant to share.'

kind:1.en: Not every *kind* of storm is born from wind and rain. Old Helm pointed at the sky, where the clouds moved in slow, tight circles rather than rushing lines. 'This one is different,' he said. Bell nodded, already adjusting our heading without being asked. I felt the air go very still.
kind:1.cnHint: 老舵长辨认出这是一种特殊____的风暴，与普通暴风截然不同。
kind:1.hook: Then the circling clouds began, slowly, to descend.
kind:1.line: 'I have never seen this *kind* of storm in all my years at sea.'

across:1.en: A narrow rope bridge stretched *across* the gap between our island and the storm-battered one ahead. The planks swung wildly in the wind. Old Helm went first, arms out for balance, moving with a calm that made the rest of us breathe again. I watched every step he took.
across:1.cnHint: 一座摇摆的绳桥横____两座岛屿，老舵长率先踏上去。
across:1.hook: Halfway over, he stopped — and looked straight down.
across:1.line: 'Once we go *across*, there is no easy way back.'

factor:1.en: Bell studied the spinning clouds and the colour of the waves for a long moment. 'Wind direction is one *factor*,' she said, 'but the temperature of the air here — feel it — that changes everything.' She was right. The cold came from below, not above. That meant the storm had a second source.
factor:1.cnHint: 领航员指出气温是判断风暴走向的一个关键____。
factor:1.hook: If there was a second source, something on the island was feeding it.
factor:1.line: 'Temperature is the one *factor* none of the old charts ever measured.'

condition:1.en: The deck was wet, the ropes were stiff, and the sky offered no clear light to steer by. In this *condition*, Old Helm said, most captains would anchor and wait. But Silverfang's ship was already moving ahead of us through the dark, and waiting meant losing the word we had come so far to find.
condition:1.cnHint: 在如此恶劣的____下，老舵长决定不停船，继续追赶竞争者。
condition:1.hook: Silverfang's lantern blinked once — then disappeared completely.
condition:1.line: 'In this *condition*, every second we wait is a second Silverfang gains.'

effort:1.en: I pulled the rope with everything I had, and still the sail barely moved. Bell appeared beside me without a word and added her strength to mine. The combined *effort* was enough — the canvas caught the wind and filled with a deep, satisfying boom. Old Helm gave a single nod of approval.
effort:1.cnHint: 我和领航员合力____，终于让船帆迎风张开。
effort:1.hook: That boom echoed back from somewhere — ahead, where no island should be.
effort:1.line: 'Your *effort* just now reminded me why I asked you to join us.'

education:1.en: The storm had torn away half the sky-bridge, leaving loose boards over a drop of nothing. Old Helm walked each plank without a tremor. 'Watch my feet, not the gap,' he said. That small lesson felt like the truest *education* the troupe had ever given me.
education:1.cnHint: 老舵手走过断裂的天桥，用行动给了我最深刻的____。
education:1.hook: One board cracked beneath my heel.
education:1.line: 'Every crossing is an *education*, if you keep your eyes open.'

scientist:1.en: Bell pulled out a brass tool and held it against the wind, counting under her breath. She tracked the storm's speed, its spin, the colour of its edges. Old Helm called her our lucky charm, but I thought she was more like a *scientist* studying a living thing.
scientist:1.cnHint: 小铃用黄铜仪器测量风暴数据，像一位____一样专注。
scientist:1.hook: Then the tool began spinning on its own.
scientist:1.line: 'A good *scientist* trusts the numbers, not the fear.'

physical:1.en: The storm wall rose ahead — a tower of spinning cloud taller than three islands stacked together. I had read about such storms in the troupe's old maps, but no ink drawing could prepare me for the raw *physical* force that pushed against my chest like an open hand.
physical:1.cnHint: 风暴那股____上的冲击力，远比地图上画的更真实可怕。
physical:1.hook: My feet left the deck for a second.
physical:1.line: 'The *physical* pressure alone can crack a mast — hold tight!'

quality:1.en: Old Helm chose our rope that morning with great care, running each metre through his fingers. 'This one has the *quality* we need,' he said, setting two cheaper coils aside. When the gust hit and the rope held us to the mast, I understood exactly what he had felt for.
quality:1.cnHint: 老舵手仔细挑选绳索的____，这根绳子后来救了大家。
quality:1.hook: The cheaper coils snapped like dry grass.
quality:1.line: 'Never trade *quality* for speed when a storm is coming.'

habit:1.en: Every morning at sea, Bell walks the full edge of the deck before breakfast. I once asked why. 'Old *habit*,' she said with a shrug. But during the storm, that same walk told her exactly which rail had come loose in the night, and she fixed it an hour before it mattered.
habit:1.cnHint: 小铃每天绕甲板走一圈的____，在风暴前夕意外救了众人。
habit:1.hook: The loose rail swung wide into grey air.
habit:1.line: 'A good *habit* costs nothing and saves everything.'

sound:1.en: The storm had its own voice — a deep, rolling *sound* that came not from any single direction but from everywhere at once, as though the sky itself were clearing its throat. We all stopped talking. Even the ropes seemed to listen before the first true gust arrived.
sound:1.cnHint: 风暴发出一种令人屏息的____，像整片天空在说话。
sound:1.hook: Then the voice dropped to a whisper.
sound:1.line: 'That *sound* means the eye is closer than the maps show.'

average:1.en: Bell checked her numbers twice and shook her head. 'This storm is moving three times faster than *average*,' she said, spreading her charts across the crate. We had planned for a slow crossing. We now had less than half the time, and the far island was still a pale dot on the horizon.
average:1.cnHint: 小铃发现风暴速度远超____水平，大家必须重新规划路线。
average:1.hook: The pale dot began to disappear into cloud.
average:1.line: 'Forget the *average* — this one plays by its own rules.'

body:1.en: The wind hit us broadside and the whole ship groaned like a tired animal. I pressed my *body* flat against the mast, arms wrapped around wood, and felt every shudder pass through my ribs. Old Helm looked almost calm, as if the storm were simply shaking hands with him.
body:1.cnHint: 我用____紧贴桅杆，感受着风暴的每一次震动。
body:1.hook: Old Helm let go of the rail and smiled.
body:1.line: 'Let your *body* find the ship's balance — fight it and you fall.'

personal:1.en: Before the storm hit, Old Helm gathered us on the deck of the sky-ship. He pulled out a small, worn notebook and said this journey was *personal* — not just for the troupe, but for a promise he had kept for twenty years. The wind sharpened around us.
personal:1.cnHint: 老舵手告诉我们，这次航行对他而言有着____的意义，与一个承诺有关。
personal:1.hook: What promise could matter so much after twenty years?
personal:1.line: 'This voyage is *personal* to me — please trust me on that.'

rather:1.en: The storm wall ahead was dark and wide. Bell studied her charts for a long moment, then looked up and said she would *rather* sail straight through the middle than go around and lose three days. Old Helm nodded slowly. I gripped the railing.
rather:1.cnHint: 领航员认为，她____选择穿越风暴中心，而不是绕行。
rather:1.hook: Straight through the middle — could any ship survive that?
rather:1.line: 'I would *rather* face the storm head-on than waste three days.'

instead:1.en: I expected Old Helm to order us to drop anchor and wait out the storm. *Instead*, he smiled, rolled up his maps, and climbed to the highest mast himself. The troupe exchanged glances. Whatever he had seen in the clouds, it was not danger.
instead:1.cnHint: 我以为老舵手会下锚等待，但他____爬上了最高的桅杆。
instead:1.hook: What had Old Helm spotted in those dark, swirling clouds?
instead:1.line: 'Do not wait — climb *instead*, and you will see what I see.'

performance:1.en: To calm the crew during the rough crossing, Bell began to sing. It started as a soft hum, but it grew into a full *performance* — voice rising above the wind, arms wide, boots tapping the wet deck. Even the storm seemed to pause and listen.
performance:1.cnHint: 为了安抚船员，领航员在甲板上献上了一场____。
performance:1.hook: Then the clouds parted, and something else was listening too.
performance:1.line: 'Every *performance* I give is for the crew — they need this now.'

percent:1.en: Old Helm checked the ship's wind-stones and shook his head. 'Fifty *percent* power left,' he said quietly. The storm was pulling energy from the stones faster than anyone had expected. We had enough to reach the next island — but only just. No room for mistakes.
percent:1.cnHint: 老舵手发现风能石只剩下五十____的能量，形势紧张。
percent:1.hook: Half power, a full storm ahead — every second counted now.
percent:1.line: 'We are at fifty *percent* — we must not waste a single breath of wind.'

achieve:1.en: Silverfang pulled his sky-ship alongside ours in the middle of the gale, shouting across the gap. He said no small troupe could *achieve* what his crew had tried and failed for years. Old Helm listened calmly, then turned back to the wheel without a word.
achieve:1.cnHint: 竞争船长嘲讽我们，说小团队不可能____他们多年未能完成的事。
achieve:1.hook: Old Helm's silence felt louder than any storm.
achieve:1.line: 'You will never *achieve* what my crew could not — sail away now.'

challenge:1.en: The narrow pass between two storm-clouds was called the Needle. Bell said crossing it was the greatest *challenge* on this sea route — the gap shifted every few minutes, and the winds inside spun in opposite directions. She took the wheel herself and did not blink.
challenge:1.cnHint: 领航员说，穿越这道被称为"针眼"的气流夹缝是此航线最大的____。
challenge:1.hook: The gap was already closing — Bell had one single chance.
challenge:1.line: 'This is the real *challenge* — and I have waited years to meet it.'

power:1.en: Deep in the storm's heart, something glowed below the clouds — a spinning column of light. Bell called it a wind-core, a knot of pure natural *power* that could refill the ship's stones in moments. Old Helm steered straight for it, and the whole sky turned white.
power:1.cnHint: 风暴中心有一股纯粹的自然____，可以为飞船补充能量。
power:1.hook: The white light swallowed us — and the ship sang like a bell.
power:1.line: 'That *power* down there belongs to the sky — let us take just enough.'

animal:0.en: Inside the storm-shelter cabin, a wooden box sat in the corner. Old Helm lifted the lid and found a small, shivering creature inside. 'Every *animal* deserves a dry place,' he said softly. We wrapped it in a spare scarf. It blinked at us with wide, calm eyes.
animal:0.cnHint: 老舵手在避风小屋里发现了一只躲雨的小____。
animal:0.hook: But the creature wore a tiny map tag around its neck.
animal:0.line: 'Every *animal* deserves a dry place,' Old Helm said softly.

goal:0.en: Bell spread the chart across the cabin table, tracing routes with one careful finger. 'Our *goal* is the Amber Shelf island,' she said, tapping a blank space on the map. The whole troupe leaned in. Outside, wind shook the walls, but inside, we had a clear direction at last.
goal:0.cnHint: 领航员在小屋里向大家说明了此行的____。
goal:0.hook: Then Bell noticed the blank space was slowly filling with new ink.
goal:0.line: 'Our *goal* is the Amber Shelf — nothing else matters right now,' Bell said.

adult:0.en: A young stowaway had hidden behind the supply crates. Old Helm knelt to his level and spoke gently. 'Being an *adult* is not about size,' he told the boy, 'it is about keeping your word.' The child nodded slowly. We gave him warm soup and a small task of his own.
adult:0.cnHint: 老舵手告诉藏在货箱后的孩子，什么才是真正的____。
adult:0.hook: The boy reached into his coat and pulled out a glowing word-shard.
adult:0.line: 'Being an *adult* is about keeping your word, not about size,' Old Helm said.

poor:0.en: Silverfang stepped into the cabin soaking wet, his fine coat dripping on the floor. He looked around at our simple lanterns and thin blankets. 'What *poor* shelter this is,' he muttered. Yet he sat down without another word, accepted a bowl of broth, and stayed until the storm passed.
poor:0.cnHint: 竞争船长进入小屋后嫌弃这里的条件____。
poor:0.hook: He left a single gold coin on the table when no one was watching.
poor:0.line: 'What *poor* shelter this is,' Silverfang muttered, then sat down anyway.

price:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a faded list of island words we still needed. Beside each word someone had written a *price* — some cost rare goods, others cost a brave act or a lost memory. I stared at the last entry. Its price was simply: one truth. That felt harder than all the rest.
price:0.cnHint: 老舵手展示的清单上，每个词旁边都标着获取它所需付出的____。
price:0.hook: The last price on the list had been crossed out and rewritten in fresh ink.
price:0.line: 'Every word has a *price* — choose carefully,' Old Helm warned us.

type:0.en: Bell sorted the word-shards into rows on the cabin floor. 'Each *type* unlocks a different island,' she explained, holding one up to the lantern light. Some glowed blue, some amber. Old Helm nodded slowly. I picked up an amber shard; it felt warm, like sunlight trapped inside cool glass.
type:0.cnHint: 领航员向大家说明，不同____的词语碎片会开启不同的岛屿。
type:0.hook: One shard in the corner glowed a colour none of us had seen before.
type:0.line: 'Each *type* unlocks a different island,' Bell explained, holding the shard up.

sense:0.en: The storm had scrambled our instruments. Silverfang pressed his palm flat on the cabin wall and closed his eyes. 'I have a *sense* that the wind is turning north,' he said quietly. We all went still. A minute later, the weather-vane above us creaked and swung — exactly north.
sense:0.cnHint: 竞争船长凭借直觉____到风向即将改变。
sense:0.hook: He opened his eyes and whispered, 'Something is guiding this storm.'
sense:0.line: 'I have a *sense* the wind is turning north,' Silverfang said quietly.

rate:0.en: Bell watched the rain streak down the cabin window, counting under her breath. 'At this *rate*,' she said, 'the storm will clear before dawn.' Old Helm checked his pocket watch and gave a small satisfied nod. We began repacking our bags. The next island was already waiting beyond the clouds.
rate:0.cnHint: 领航员根据雨势的____判断风暴将在黎明前结束。
rate:0.hook: Then the rain stopped — two full hours earlier than Bell had expected.
rate:0.line: 'At this *rate*, we will reach clear skies before dawn,' Bell said.

key:1.en: The docking post was sealed with a heavy iron lock. Old Helm reached into his coat and pulled out a small, bright object. 'This,' he said, holding it up against the starlight, 'is the *key* to the storm channel. Without it, we go nowhere.'
key:1.cnHint: 老舵手从外套里取出一个小东西，说它是通往风暴航道的____。
key:1.hook: But the lock had already been forced open.
key:1.line: 'This is the *key* to the storm channel, and someone else wants it.'

issue:1.en: Bell spread the old chart across the barrel top. A torn edge cut right through the marked route. 'That gap is the real *issue*,' she said, tracing the missing section with one finger. 'We cannot sail blind into storm water.' Old Helm nodded slowly and said nothing.
issue:1.cnHint: 领航员指着海图上的缺口，说这才是真正的____所在。
issue:1.hook: Someone had torn that section away on purpose.
issue:1.line: 'The torn chart is the *issue*; without it, we are flying blind.'

against:1.en: Wind struck the platform hard, and Bell leaned *against* the tall wooden post to keep her balance. Ropes snapped like whips overhead. 'Storm is early!' Old Helm shouted across the noise. Loose crates slid toward the edge. I grabbed the nearest one and held on, heart loud in my chest.
against:1.cnHint: 风暴提前来临，领航员____着木柱才没被吹倒。
against:1.hook: Then the post itself began to crack.
against:1.line: 'Lean *against* the mast and do not let go, not yet.'

matter:1.en: Silverfang blocked our path at the bridge gate, arms folded. 'This is a private dock,' he said. Old Helm looked him in the eye. 'The *matter* before us is bigger than any one dock or crew. A storm word is loose out there, and it belongs to no one captain.' Silverfang did not move.
matter:1.cnHint: 银牙拦住去路，老舵手说眼前的____比任何一个船长都重要。
matter:1.hook: Silverfang's hand moved slowly toward the gate latch.
matter:1.line: 'This *matter* is bigger than your dock, Silverfang, much bigger.'

raise:1.en: Old Helm planted his feet at the cliff edge and looked out at the grey clouds rolling in. 'We *raise* the signal flag now,' he said, 'or the supply boats will turn back and we lose the whole crossing.' Bell ran for the pole. I helped her pull the rope, hand over hand.
raise:1.cnHint: 老舵手命令大家____信号旗，否则补给船会掉头离开。
raise:1.hook: The flag went up just as lightning split the sky.
raise:1.line: '*Raise* the flag now, or the supply boats will never find us.'

option:1.en: The bridge ahead had cracked down the middle. Going back meant three extra hours through the storm belt. Old Helm stood still for a moment. 'Our only *option*,' he said at last, 'is the rope bridge lower on the cliff.' Bell looked down at the fog far below and took a breath.
option:1.cnHint: 桥断了，老舵手说绕道太久，唯一的____是去悬崖下的绳桥。
option:1.hook: The rope bridge was already swaying in the wind.
option:1.line: 'The rope bridge is our only *option*, so we take it now.'

society:1.en: A carved stone sign stood at the island's entrance gate. Bell read it aloud: 'Here the Chart-Keeper's *Society* once kept every sea word ever found.' Old Helm ran his hand along the cold stone. 'They're gone now,' he said quietly. 'But the words they kept are still here, waiting.'
society:1.cnHint: 石碑上写着，这里曾是一个保存所有海图词语的____的旧址。
society:1.hook: A light still burned inside the empty hall.
society:1.line: 'The Chart-Keeper's *Society* built this place; their words are still inside.'

whole:1.en: I climbed to the top of the watchtower and looked out. The storm wrapped around the *whole* island like a grey wall, closing every direction at once. There was no clear sky in any direction. Old Helm stood beside me and said, calm as ever, 'Then we find the eye, and we sail through it.'
whole:1.cnHint: 我爬上了瞭望塔，发现风暴把____岛屿都包围了。
whole:1.hook: Somewhere inside that grey wall, a light was moving.
whole:1.line: 'The storm has taken the *whole* island; our way out is through the centre.'

nearly:1.en: The storm hit without warning. Our little ship tipped so far that I *nearly* fell into the open sky below. Old Helm grabbed a rope and pulled me back to the deck. The floating island ahead was still hidden behind walls of grey cloud.
nearly:1.cnHint: 暴风雨突袭，我____从船边跌落星空之下。
nearly:1.hook: But the rope was already starting to fray.
nearly:1.line: 'We *nearly* lost you to that drop,' Old Helm said quietly.

wrong:1.en: Bell spread the map across the wet deck and shook her head. 'Something is *wrong*,' she said. The star markers on the map pointed east, but every wind we could feel pushed firmly west. Old Helm looked at the sky and stayed silent for a long moment.
wrong:1.cnHint: 领航员发现地图上有____，星标与风向完全相反。
wrong:1.hook: One of them — the map or the sky — was lying.
wrong:1.line: 'The direction is *wrong*; east and west do not match here.'

variety:1.en: When the storm calmed, we landed on a small island market floating just below the clouds. A *variety* of island traders had gathered here, selling coloured spices, tiny lanterns, and jars of cloud-water. Old Helm moved through the stalls slowly, reading every label with care.
variety:1.cnHint: 风暴平息后，我们在一座市集岛上看到____各异的商品。
variety:1.hook: One jar held something that moved on its own.
variety:1.line: 'A *variety* of goods like this means many islands feed this place.'

clear:1.en: The storm thinned at last, and the view became *clear* — a chain of five islands hung in the distance like lanterns on a string. Bell marked each one on our map with a small cross. Old Helm stood at the bow and counted them twice under his breath.
clear:1.cnHint: 风暴散去，远处的岛链变得____可见，贝尔迅速标注在地图上。
clear:1.hook: Five islands — but the map had only shown four.
clear:1.line: 'Now the path is *clear*; we follow the chain north.'

gain:1.en: Old Helm traded three jars of spice with a cloud-fisher and came back smiling. Our *gain* from the deal was a torn piece of sky-chart showing a hidden passage through the storm belt. Bell pressed it flat beside our own map and let out a soft, happy sound.
gain:1.cnHint: 团长以香料换取了一张残图，这次交换的____是一条隐秘航路。
gain:1.hook: The passage had a warning scrawled across it in red.
gain:1.line: 'Every *gain* on this journey begins with a trade,' Old Helm said.

maybe:1.en: Silverfang's ship appeared out of the grey cloud on our left side. She waved, which surprised me. '*Maybe* she wants to call a truce while the storm lasts,' Bell said, watching carefully. Old Helm did not wave back yet; he simply kept both hands on the wheel and waited.
maybe:1.cnHint: 银牙船长突然现身并招手，贝尔猜测她____是想暂时休战。
maybe:1.hook: Then Silverfang pointed — at something behind us.
maybe:1.line: '*Maybe* this once we sail together and argue later,' Silverfang called.

huge:1.en: A wave of wind — solid as a wall — rolled across the sky and struck our ship from below. The boom was *huge*, loud enough to silence every voice on deck. For a second, the whole island chain ahead shook like leaves. Then everything went still and oddly quiet.
huge:1.cnHint: 一道巨大的气浪袭来，那声____震响让甲板上所有人瞬间沉默。
huge:1.hook: In that quiet, we heard something else — something below.
huge:1.line: 'That *huge* sound came from the deep cloud layer,' Bell whispered.

diet:1.en: While we waited for the wind to settle, Old Helm handed everyone a small biscuit and dried fruit. 'Cloud travel changes your *diet*,' he said cheerfully. 'Heavy food makes you slow when the ship tips.' I ate the biscuit and looked out at the silver-edged clouds ahead.
diet:1.cnHint: 团长解释说，云上航行会改变旅人的____，要以轻食为主。
diet:1.hook: Beyond those clouds, something glowed a deep, hungry red.
diet:1.line: 'A light *diet* keeps a sailor sharp when the sky turns rough.'

animal:1.en: The storm island market was loud and full of life. Every trader kept at least one creature nearby — for luck, they said. Bell stopped beside a cage where a feathered *animal* with bright eyes watched the clouds like it was reading them. 'That one knows the wind better than I do,' she whispered. Old Helm dropped a coin on the counter without a word.
animal:1.cnHint: 贝尔在市场上注意到一只笼中的____，觉得它似乎能读懂风向。
animal:1.hook: The creature's feathers suddenly stood on end.
animal:1.line: 'That *animal* has been watching the storm gate for an hour,' said Bell.

goal:1.en: Rain hammered the dock as we tied up the ship. Old Helm spread the word-map on a wet barrel and tapped the far edge. 'Every step we take has one *goal*,' he said, voice steady over the thunder, 'and that is the island behind the lightning wall.' I stared at the blank space on the map and felt my heart lift instead of sink.
goal:1.cnHint: 老舵手在暴风雨中指着地图，说明队伍此行的____。
goal:1.hook: Behind the lightning wall, something was already moving.
goal:1.line: 'Our *goal* is that island — nothing else matters tonight,' said Old Helm.

adult:1.en: The storm had knocked out the market lamps and the youngest crew member, a boy named Pip, was trying to fix them alone. Old Helm watched for a moment, then stepped back. 'Let him work,' he told me quietly. 'Every *adult* on this ship learned by doing the hard thing first.' Pip got the last lamp burning just as the rain stopped.
adult:1.cnHint: 老舵手让小水手独自修灯，说每个____都是这样历练出来的。
adult:1.hook: The lamp light caught something written on the wall behind Pip.
adult:1.line: 'Every *adult* here earned their place by doing it the hard way,' said Old Helm.

poor:1.en: A trader at the dock shook his head when we asked about the word fragment. '*Poor* map readers end up on the reef,' he said, not unkindly, pointing to a line of broken ships below the cliffs. Bell spread our word-map on his counter. He looked at it a long moment, then his eyes went wide and his tone changed completely.
poor:1.cnHint: 码头商人警告说，____的地图阅读者会触礁——但随后他看到了我们的地图。
poor:1.hook: His finger trembled as it touched the map's edge.
poor:1.line: '*Poor* readers of the wind end up down there,' the trader said, pointing at the reef.

price:1.en: The old chart-seller on the storm dock had exactly the fragment we needed, folded inside a glass bottle. 'Every word has a *price*,' she said, setting it on the counter between us. She did not ask for coins. She asked for a story. Old Helm sat down on a wet crate, cleared his throat, and began to speak. By the end, she handed over the bottle herself.
price:1.cnHint: 卖图老人说每个词都有____，但她想要的不是钱，而是一个故事。
price:1.hook: The fragment inside the bottle glowed faintly as Old Helm spoke.
price:1.line: 'Every word has a *price*, and I decide what that is,' said the chart-seller.

type:1.en: Bell laid three word fragments side by side on the ship's rail and studied them in the storm light. 'There is a *type* of island that only appears during thunder season,' she said, tracing the shapes with one finger. 'These three pieces together describe exactly that kind of place.' A low rumble crossed the sky, and her eyes lit up.
type:1.cnHint: 贝尔研究碎片后说，它们描述的是某种特定____的岛屿，只在雷雨季节出现。
type:1.hook: Thunder rolled, and a new shape rose through the clouds ahead.
type:1.line: 'This *type* of island only shows itself when lightning touches the sea,' said Bell.
